clue.text: Revival of Cantona clique with little advertisement: he goes back a long way

definitions.text: he goes back a long way

indicators.note: a revival brings the words back in a new production, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: AD is the short form of advertisement

explanation.surface: A footballer's old gang staging a comeback, with a small advert, is someone with a long history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revival of' rearranges CANTONA CLIQUE together with AD. Eric Cantona is the French footballer famous at Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone you have known for many years is a person who goes back a long way with you; the phrase also opens the famous Burns song.

clue.text: Observe article in a very bad temper

parts.note: to observe is to see
an article is an item, a thing

explanation.surface: Watching an item while in a foul mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' wants to be A, AN or THE; here it is the general sense of an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is fuming with suppressed anger is said to be inwardly boiling, an idiom for being furious.

clue.text: Streams of fire?

parts.note: Scots word for small streams, which also names the injuries fire inflicts, and the national poet whose night the puzzle celebrates

explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland small streams are so called, and the same word describes what fire does to skin; the poet Robert of that name fits the theme.

clue.text: Swineherd's agreement to celebration

parts.note: a swineherd is a man who tends hogs, a hog man
AY (aye) is an old word of assent, yes

explanation.surface: A pig-keeper agreeing to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's links the swineherd to the agreement. HOGMANAY is the Scottish New Year's Eve celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish New Year's Eve festivities are a famous national celebration with parties and singing.

clue.text: Sound from the mouth of a prude in the corn

indicators.note: the clue asks for what is heard, so the word is spoken and spelt differently

parts.words: from the mouth of a prude
parts.note: a prude is mealy-mouthed, unwilling to speak plainly

explanation.surface: A prim person murmuring something in a cornfield.
explanation.walkthrough: A prude is 'mealy-mouthed', so what comes from such a mouth is mealy, which is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa maize is called by this word, so it is a regional name for corn.

clue.text: POW's hello out of Powys

indicators.note: letters knocked out of place are rearranged, so the words are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written, its apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war's greeting coming from the Welsh county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges POWS HELLO. Powys is a county in mid Wales, and the answer is one of its market towns.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a market town in the Welsh county of Powys, so it belongs to that county.

clue.text: The man's eating a horse said to be from a sheep

definitions.text: said to be from a sheep

indicators.note: one piece eats another, taking it inside

parts.note: his means belonging to the man
GG, gee-gee, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A man munching on horsemeat that is claimed to be mutton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said to be' hedges because the Scottish dish is made from sheep's offal, though jokes claim it is a wild creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish pudding is made from sheep's heart, liver and lungs, so it is reputed to come from a sheep.

clue.text: End of 3 night and 4? Don't forget 1

definitions.text: End of 3 night and 4? Don't forget 1

parts.words: End of 3 night and 4? Don't forget 1
parts.note: the song sung at the close of the poet's night and of the Scottish New Year, whose first line says old friends should not be forgotten

explanation.definitionFit: The Burns song traditionally ends both Burns Night and Hogmanay and opens by asking whether old friends should be forgot.

clue.text: Report of holiday you forfeit requires sugar

indicators.note: a report is what is heard, so the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: holiday is leave, and to forfeit is to lose: leave you lose

explanation.surface: Annual leave that goes unused means having to take some sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'leave you lose' runs together as the name of the sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Laevulose is an old name for fructose, the fruit sugar.

clue.text: Period given to or taken from 20

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A period of time given to, or taken from, something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself a puzzle: 20 is MOUSER, and taking OR from it leaves MUSE. Erato is one of the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric poetry, and a Muse is what remains when OR is removed from the cat at 20.

clue.text: Oppo, perhaps, of Caesar, J?

parts.note: an opposite word, 'oppo' for short; Julius Caesar's 'oppo' (partner) was Mark Antony, written in surname-first style as ...

explanation.definitionFit: A word of opposite meaning is called this, and Caesar's sidekick Antony, M fits the letters when listed surname first.

clue.text: Italian strips to decline being captured by Turner

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another, captured within it

parts.note: Lana Turner was the Hollywood film star
to sag is to decline or droop

explanation.surface: Italian lines of resistance collapsing when caught by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the English painter; it is the actress Lana Turner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagna is pasta made in broad flat sheets, Italian strips of dough.

clue.text: A pound of tobacco

explanation.surface: Someone buying a pound's weight of tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a pound sterling, and also a plug of tobacco held in the cheek for chewing.

clue.text: Trial opens with resolution of parenthesis

indicators.note: resolving something breaks it into parts and reworks it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A court case begins with a ruling on an aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' rearranges TRIAL OPENS.
explanation.definitionFit: A parenthesis is a remark put in between others, an interposal or insertion.

clue.text: Isaac in relation to Dingle, Hugh, Michael and Paul, for 4

definitions.text: Isaac in relation to Dingle, Hugh, Michael and Paul, for 4

parts.words: Isaac in relation to Dingle, Hugh, Michael and Paul, for 4
parts.note: Isaac Foot was the father of the Foot brothers, so the earliest of that family; and the Scottish New Year custom of being the year's first visitor

explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Foot, Liberal MP, fathered Dingle, Hugh and Michael Foot; Paul Foot was his grandson. At Hogmanay the first visitor across the threshold is so called.
explanation.definitionFit: At Hogmanay the first person to cross a threshold after midnight is the first-foot, and Isaac was the patriarch of the Foot dynasty.

clue.text: Most of an earthly paradise sadly ends in bad temper

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, its outer pieces cut away

parts.note: Shangri-La is the paradise on earth in Hilton's novel

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A paradise on earth ending gloomily in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims SH and A from SHANGRILA to leave ANGRIL; 'ends' gives Y, the last letter of 'sadly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something angrily means doing it with a bad temper, an adverb of manner.

clue.text: King entering sound asleep left for a breather

parts.note: to snore is the sound made when asleep
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch walks in on a sleeper, then leaves for some fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound asleep' looks like 'deeply asleep'; here it is the noise a sleeper makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A snorkel is a tube that lets a swimmer breathe underwater, a breathing device.

clue.text: Taylor is inclined to be on his tod

indicators.note: letters set on a slant are moved out of line, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mr Taylor tends to keep himself to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclined' rearranges TAYLOR IS. 'On his tod' is British slang (rhyming slang Tod Sloan = own) for on his own.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's tod is British slang for being alone, which is what solitary means.

clue.text: Cup of milk for human 8?

parts.note: the Burns song at 8 offers 'a cup o'' this quality, and Shakespeare's phrase speaks of the milk of human ...

explanation.definitionFit: The Burns song promises a cup o' kindness, and Macbeth speaks of the milk of human kindness: both describe benevolence.

clue.text: Miners shift bulks for pounds, the fools

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers

indicators.note: to shift the word is to move its letters about

parts.note: LS, from Latin librae, is the abbreviation for pounds

explanation.surface: Coal workers moving loads for money are idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a miner's work period; it rearranges BULKS to BSKUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbskulls are stupid people, so the word is a plain synonym of fools.

clue.text: Cat employing doctor?

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
one employing something is a user of it

explanation.surface: A cat that calls in the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as MO user: one who employs a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat kept for catching mice, a common name for such a pet.

clue.text: Green and pure in effect

indicators.note: putting something into effect works it into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Being green and naive works out as purity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effect' rearranges PURE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Green fruit is fruit that is not yet ripe, so green is a synonym for immature.

clue.text: A refusal from Chirac or person unknown?

parts.note: non is French for no, as the French president would say

explanation.surface: A French president turning someone down, or a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Chirac was President of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, used to sign work by someone whose name is not known.

clue.text: Melody canonised in flight?

parts.note: a canonised person is a saint, ST
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A tune declared holy while on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: A saint's title goes before the name, so the canonised tune takes the saint's abbreviation in front. 'flight' suggests flying; it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step is one unit in a flight of stairs, so it is found in a flight.

clue.text: As the Welsh might say, like an aspen where there's water

indicators.note: a Welsh accent is imagined voicing the word, so the spoken form stands in

parts.note: aspens are proverbial for trembling leaves, so like one is aquiver

explanation.surface: Welsh people describing something trembling like an aspen near water.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a Welsh accent turns the V of 'aquiver' into an F.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquifer is underground rock holding water, a natural reservoir.

clue.text: Taste unaltered by mandibular paralysis?

indicators.note: altered letters are changed in order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the first two letters of unaltered

explanation.surface: Flavour unchanged by a stiffened jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unaltered' must be read as 'un altered': UN joins TASTE as fodder and 'altered' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is also called lockjaw because it makes the jaw muscles seize up.

clue.text: Left infirm by faith?

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a red is a socialist, someone on the political left

explanation.surface: Someone left infirm and weak by their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infirm' must be split into 'in firm': the communist colour sits inside the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of belief, a creed, so it names a faith.

clue.text: Leave car at home, taking issue with lawman

parts.note: to park is to leave a car
in means at home
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: Parking at home and arguing with a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lawman' suggests a sheriff; it is C. Northcote Parkinson, who coined Parkinson's Law that work expands to fill the time available.
explanation.definitionFit: C. Northcote Parkinson formulated the law named after him, so he is a man known for a law.
